label: copy-phase fed-back "0" late in long sequences (next output z/b/h/j/f/e/0)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of mass), almost always when the fed-back input token is the digit 0 (97% of mass, 94% of active steps). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or at recall_idx <= 2. Rate climbs steeply with position: recall_idx 3 gives 0.2x lift, recall_idx 8 gives 14x; it is mostly in L=8-9 sequences, near the end (to_go 0-1). Magnitude also depends on the token being output next: z, 0, b, h, j, f, e give the highest rates, while v, 2, t, n, o rarely fire. The top activations (~3.5) are input 0 at the second-to-last or last copy step with z or b output next. The bare rule in_tok==0 in the copy phase has 0.94 recall but only 0.09 precision, because most late 0 inputs do not fire. Requiring recall_idx>=5 and an out_tok from the favoured set gives precision 0.67 but recall 0.51 (dev). Small leftover activations happen on inputs z/h/j/f in the late copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: 0, z, h, f, j, b; least: s, d, n, i) and the token being output (most: z, 0, h, b, j, f; least: p, a, t, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=7, t=15, recall_idx=6.
